title: 1995 AHSME Problem 20
statement: If \(a,\) \(b\) and \(c\) are three (not necessarily different) numbers chosen randomly and with replacement from the set \(\{1,2,3,4,5\},\) the probability that \(ab+c\) is even is

solutions.text: There are \(3\) odd and \(2\) even choices. The product \(ab\) is odd with probability \(\frac{9}{25}\) and even with probability \(\frac{16}{25}.\) Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} P(ab+c\text{ even}) &=\frac9{25}\cdot\frac35\\ &\quad{}+\frac{16}{25}\cdot\frac25\\ &=\frac{59}{125}. \end{aligned} \] Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: The sum is even when \(ab\) and \(c\) have the same parity
The product \(ab\) is odd only when both selected factors are odd
